s: A company is modernizing a legacy.NET Framework application backed by SQL Server. Requirements: Containerize into microservices. Control OS patches and storage. Add load balancing. Ensure high availability. Which solution meets all of these with minimal refactoring?
o: Use App2Container to deploy on ECS EC2 with ALB and RDS for SQL Server.
Use App2Container on ECS EC2 with NLB and Aurora MySQL.
Use Porting Assistant and EKS with Fargate and Aurora MySQL.
Use Porting Assistant and EKS with Fargate and RDS SQL Server.
e: A is correct because: App2Containersupports packaging .NET Framework apps into containers without porting to .NET Core. ECS with EC2 gives full control over the OS and patching. ALB handles microservice-level load balancing. RDS for SQL Server with Multi-AZ ensures high availability. Options B, C, and D involve Aurora MySQL (incompatible with SQL Server features) or require .NET Core, which involves more significant application changes. Reference: App2Container Overview ECS EC2 vs Fargate

w.y: The deciding words are 'control OS patches and storage', 'load balancing', and 'minimal refactoring' for a .NET Framework app on SQL Server. App2Container containerizes the app without code changes, ECS on EC2 keeps control of the host OS, an ALB balances HTTP traffic, and RDS for SQL Server keeps the same database engine.

o.A: Correct: App2Container plus ECS on EC2, an ALB, and RDS for SQL Server meets every requirement with little refactoring.
o.B: Moving from SQL Server to Aurora MySQL needs schema and code changes.
o.C: Fargate gives no control of the OS, and Aurora MySQL means a database rewrite.
o.D: Fargate gives no control of the OS, and Porting Assistant targets .NET Core porting, which is more refactoring.

st: Right for the exam; App2Container is closed to new customers and AWS now points to AWS Transform.
